result.target: SCOPE STRICTLY to git diff 9c3b4513b^..9c3b4513b -- the round-7 FIX for the INF advisor-of-record detect-and-alert monitor. Files: data/inf/scripts/gold/lib/aor_attribution_audit.py (main restructured into _run_spot_check + _emit_alert; a freshness gate; every non-green routed as a FINDING-grade alert), data/inf/scripts/gold/INF_A_01.advisor_assignments.py (skip emit + LOUD WARN on blank-raw; date comparison to SOURCE as-of not wall-clock), + the test file. IGNORE ALL uncommitted working-tree changes to any OTHER file (out of scope). CONTEXT: the prior review (wjlqray4r) found the detector SILENTLY FALSE-GREENS when today's comparison partition is missing/stale/blank -- it printed 'OK: no drift' diffing two PRIOR-day partitions on a check that never ran (the non-fatal emit failed to land today's partition). This fix adds: a FRESHNESS gate (the latest partition MUST == the expected run as-of=INF_AOR_ASOF/wall-clock, else COMPARISON-STALE); a failed LIST/READ/detect -> CANNOT-EVALUATE; and CRITICALLY every non-green (stale/missing/blank/error) is a FINDING-grade AOR-DRIFT-ALERT emitted through the channel+SNS, NEVER a silent WARN in a try/except. INF_A_01 SKIPS the emit + WARNs LOUD if accounts_v2 has no populated advisor_of_record_raw (-> the detector reads a MISSING today-partition -> COMPARISON-STALE, visible, never silently-blank) + dates the comparison to the SOURCE as-of. + build_attribution_comparison is now index-KEYED (reindex servicing_key onto df.index, not positional). REVIEW BAR = the ALERT bar (detect+surface+doesn't-block+doesn't-silently-pass), NOT provable-completeness -- a missed detector edge is a NOTE. The ONLY blockers are (X) a false-green / whole-class silent-pass, or (Y) the detector BLOCKS/aborts the nightly, or (Z) a healthy day that now FALSE-ALERTS every run (placebo-fire = alert-fatigue, its own silent-absent-safety failure). VERIFY (report any NEW regression the fix introduced with HIGHEST priority): (1) does the FRESHNESS gate genuinely ALERT (COMPARISON-STALE / CANNOT-EVALUATE / COMPARISON-INCOMPLETE, FINDING-grade, through _emit_alert -> stdout token + SNS) on a MISSING-today (M1), STALE-today (M2), and BLANK-RAW (M3) partition -- NOT a false-green 'OK no drift'? (2) is EVERY non-green truly finding-grade -- confirm no path swallows a stale/missing/blank/error condition as a silent WARN inside a try/except instead of alerting. (3) is exit-0-always STILL preserved -- the alert is EMITTED but the nightly is NOT blocked/aborted (no new raise path)? (4) did the restructure (main -> _run_spot_check + _emit_alert) or the freshness gate introduce a NEW regression -- a healthy/identical day that now FALSE-ALERTS on every run (a placebo-fire that trains alert-fatigue), or a broken import/dangling ref? (5) index-keying [9-11] -- servicing_key correctly joined PER-ACCOUNT by index, no off-by-one/misalignment vs the prior positional bug. (6) EDGE 3 (per-account raw relabel reusing existing labels, no aor shift) is surfaced. (7) any REMAINING silent-false-green or silent-pass path. Ground findings against source. Switch is OFF -- rank correctness of the daily-ACTIVE detect-and-alert path.
result.summary: This diff adds an AoR-attribution drift monitor (INF_A_01 emit + INF_D_11 detector via aor_attribution_audit.py); its round-7 switch to dating the comparison partition by the source as-of (INF_AOR_ASOF) rather than wall-clock is the dominant defect, producing two false-GREEN silent-miss classes — an overwrite/collapse of the diffable baseline when the as-of repeats, and a date-label freshness gate that greens a stale or frozen partition — plus a family of false-ALERT placebo COMPARISON-STALE fires when the recomputed `expected` diverges from the partition actually written. Separately, EDGE-3 over-fires on non-meaningful raw transitions (blank->populated coverage bursts and cosmetic reformatting), a non-canonical date string permanently mismatches the lister regex, and error handling now pages Andrew on transient S3 blips. Merged the five duplicate placebo-stale restatements into [2], paired the two as-of-dating and two freshness-gate variants, and folded the cosmetic EDGE-3 case into the coverage-burst finding; kept the date-canonicalization, transient-page, and redundant-computation findings distinct.

findings.summary: Dating the comparison partition to INF_AOR_ASOF (the accounts_v2 as-of) instead of wall-clock collapses consecutive nightly emits onto ONE partition key whenever the upstream as-of repeats, and the detector then false-greens it as a baseline day. [same root cause also at: data/inf/scripts/gold/lib/aor_attribution_audit.py:387]
findings.failure_scenario: accounts_v2 is frozen at as-of 2026-07-11 for two nights (a documented, realistic freeze; the dispatch pins INF_AOR_ASOF to the LATEST accounts_v2 partition, which does not advance). Night 1 writes .../2026-07-11/data.parquet (content C1). Night 2 a roster/ADVISOR_OF_RECORD_EXPLICIT/fold-code edit re-attributes accounts -> fold produces C2 (a real per-account swap) but the emit OVERWRITES the same 2026-07-11 partition. The detector sees dates=['2026-07-11'], dates[-1]==expected -> freshness PASSES, then len(dates)<2 -> prints 'OK: baseline day, nothing to compare' and emits NO alert. The re-attribution reaches served output UNSURFACED -- exactly the never-widen/visibility gap this monitor exists to close. Old wall-clock dating wrote a distinct advancing partition every night, so the same change was always diffable.

findings.summary: The freshness gate keys on the partition's DATE LABEL (dates[-1]==expected), not on whether tonight's emit actually ran; when accounts_v2's as-of (INF_AOR_ASOF) does not advance night-over-night, a same-dated partition left by the PRIOR run satisfies the gate and greens even though tonight's INF_A_01 emit failed/was skipped. [same root cause also at: data/inf/scripts/gold/lib/aor_attribution_audit.py:375]
findings.failure_scenario: On a weekend/holiday/upstream-lag night where INF_AOR_ASOF repeats (e.g. stays 2026-07-11 two nights), INF_A_01's comparison emit fails or hits the blank-raw skip (both caught as a non-fatal WARN at INF_A_01.py:218, no new write, and save_comparison writes a fixed key {prefix}{as_of}/data.parquet so last night's file remains). INF_D_11 lists dates, dates[-1]=='2026-07-11'==expected, the gate PASSES and loads the STALE prior partition -> prints 'OK ... FRESH + no drift'. If a roster re-designation (ADVISOR_OF_RECORD_EXPLICIT / fold overlay) changed the served attribution between those nights without an as-of bump, the real per-account AoR change reaches production served data with NO AOR-DRIFT-ALERT/SNS -- the emit failure is visible only as a swallowed WARN in INF_A_01's log, exactly the silent-WARN-swallow class the fix set out to close. The comment's promise ('emit failed -> latest is an OLD partition -> STALE') holds only when the as-of advanced.

findings.summary: EDGE-3 (ACCOUNT-RAW-RELABEL-NO-SHIFT) fires on blank->populated (and populated->blank) raw transitions, not only true value-to-value relabels, because it only excludes the both-blank case. [same root cause also at: data/inf/scripts/gold/lib/aor_attribution_audit.py:245]
findings.failure_scenario: On a nightly where the roster source begins populating udf7ADVISOROF for N previously-blank accounts (a raw-coverage INCREASE, which SOURCE-DRIFT only guards on the DROP side) and none of those accounts' served aor moves, the condition `tr != yr and not (both blank) and t_aor==y_aor` is true for every one of them, so the detector emits N ACCOUNT-RAW-RELABEL-NO-SHIFT findings and an N-line SNS/SMS body in a single run -- an alert burst on a benign coverage-improvement day.

findings.summary: Because `expected` is recomputed from INF_AOR_ASOF/wall-clock rather than read from the latest emitted partition, running the detector OUTSIDE the dispatch (standalone INF_D_11 with INF_AOR_ASOF unset in the shell) makes expected=wall-clock-today while the newest partition on S3 was written by the last in-chain run dated to the (typically T-1/T-2 lagged) source as-of. [same root cause also at: data/inf/scripts/gold/lib/aor_attribution_audit.py:432, data/inf/scripts/gold/lib/aor_attribution_audit.py:432, data/inf/scripts/gold/lib/aor_attribution_audit.py:432, data/inf/scripts/gold/lib/aor_attribution_audit.py:432, data/inf/scripts/gold/lib/aor_attribution_audit.py:432]
findings.failure_scenario: An operator ad-hoc-invokes `python INF_D_11.aor_attribution_drift.py` to sanity-check the monitor with INF_AOR_ASOF unset; expected=2026-07-13 but the freshest S3 partition is 2026-07-11 (normal INF lag) -> dates[-1] != expected -> COMPARISON-STALE alert fires on every such manual check, so the human sees a spurious 'today's comparison is MISSING/STALE' alert for data that is actually current and may distrust or silence the alert.

findings.summary: The freshness gate compares date STRINGS (`dates[-1] != expected`) and `_list_comparison_dates` only matches a strict `\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}` regex, so a non-canonical (e.g. non-zero-padded) INF_AOR_ASOF permanently mismatches the partition name and fires COMPARISON-STALE every run.
findings.failure_scenario: A dispatch that pins INF_AOR_ASOF='2026-7-13' (no zero-pad) makes INF_A_01 write key .../2026-7-13/data.parquet, which the lister's `(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})` regex silently drops; dates is then empty/missing-today while expected='2026-7-13', so COMPARISON-STALE fires on every nightly run despite a written, fresh partition -- a permanent placebo-fire / alert-fatigue, and the partition is also invisible to any later day-over-day diff.

findings.summary: The removed silent-WARN-on-transient-error path is now a finding-grade CANNOT-EVALUATE routed through _publish_sns_alert, so any transient S3 blip fires a real SMS to Andrew.
findings.failure_scenario: A transient ListObjectsV2/GetObject throttle or timeout on an otherwise-healthy nightly raises inside _run_spot_check; main()'s except emits CANNOT-EVALUATE via _emit_alert -> _publish_sns_alert -> SMS to Andrew (INF_AOR_DRIFT_SNS_ARN set in prod). Recurring transient AWS errors thus produce recurring AOR-DRIFT-ALERT SMS on healthy nights, training alert-fatigue on the channel (the old code logged a WARN and never paged). Design-intended per 'couldn't-check != no-drift', but the every-transient-error paging is a new user-visible behavior.

findings.summary: EDGE-3 rebuilds t_raw/y_raw with a second _keyed() pass over the raw column that _detect_source_drift already computed for the same today/yesterday frames, and re-defines the _blank constant.
findings.failure_scenario: Every nightly run walks the entire raw udf7ADVISOROF column twice (once inside _detect_source_drift at lines 156-157, again at lines 240-241) to build identical {account_id->raw} dicts, plus a duplicated _blank set literal. Redundant O(n) work and a copy-paste constant that can drift out of sync between the two blank-sets if one is later edited; the cheaper form computes t_raw/y_raw once and threads them through, or folds EDGE-3 into the existing source-drift pass.

refuted.summary: Freshness gate keys on INF_AOR_ASOF coordination between two separate processes; a monitor step that does not inherit the exact same env value the emit used fires COMPARISON-STALE on every healthy run (perpetual placebo).
yest_d = dates[-2] is the second-newest partition, not the true prior calendar day; when an intermediate partition is missing the diff silently spans multiple days.

The removed positional '.values' assembly tolerated a non-unique df index; the new serv.reindex(df.index) raises on a duplicate index, silently disabling the emit and pinning the monitor to perpetual COMPARISON-STALE.

The new index-keyed `serv...reindex(df.index)` raises ValueError on a duplicate df index (the old positional `.values` assembly was immune); the INF_A_01 emit try/except swallows it, so a benign non-unique index produces no partition and a spurious downstream COMPARISON-STALE.

The rebuilt index-keyed assembly calls `serv.reindex(df.index)` and `pd.DataFrame({...}, index=df.index)`, which raise ValueError on a non-unique df index; the prior positional `.values` assembly tolerated duplicate index labels.
Redundant pd.Series(...) wrap around an object that is already a Series in the blank-raw check.

The blank-raw condition is guarded at two layers with two different alert codes; the detector's COMPARISON-INCOMPLETE branch is effectively unreachable given INF_A_01 already skips emitting a blank-raw partition (which surfaces as COMPARISON-STALE instead).
